body:
**Blocking.** A wipe can still report an unqualified success over blocks the card claims, that were never cleared, and that are named nowhere.

`cfa1b37f` added a floor whose premise is that the advertised count is evidence a block exists -- "the card itself says those blocks exist" (`:788`). This drop's premise is that a block answering nothing does not exist. Below `advertised` those contradict, and the drop wins.

Trace. 64-block card, advertised 64, blocks 20..63 answer neither a write nor a read (a coupling degradation that doesn't recover inside the range, or a read-protected block range):

- 20..26 set bits, `absent_run` 1..7, `continue`
- 27: `absent_run == 8`, `block + 1 == 28 < 64`, presence check passes, `continue`
- ...through 62; `absent_run == 43`, presence re-checked at 35 and 43, both pass
- 63: `absent_run == 44`, `block + 1 == 64`, so the break is now permitted. `card_still_present` passes. The re-probe at `:831` uses `read_block` -- which is what already failed -- so `still_absent == 44`. Break at `block == 64`.
- this loop clears bits 20..63; `blocks_total = highest_present + 1 = 20`; `clone_failed_count == 0`

-> `Iso15693PollerEventSuccess`. Screen: `sequence_success`, **"Wipe complete"**, "Cleared 20 blocks. / Card claims 64.", a lone `Finish`, no Details. 44 blocks still hold the previous card's data and read fine once the card is reseated.

The obvious fix -- don't drop below `advertised` -- re-breaks the 66-advertised/64-physical card you defended, which would go back to "not cleared: 2".

The discriminator is already in this file, and it is the *safe* direction of the inference `:749-755` warns about. That note says activation's block read stops at the first failure and zero-fills the rest, so the cache can't prove a block is empty. It can prove the opposite: **non-zero in the activation cache is a one-way proof that the block existed and held data.** Blocks 64/65 of the fake-flash card failed the activation read and sit there as zeros; blocks 20..63 of the degraded card were read cleanly at activation and sit there as their real contents.

So before dropping a run member below `advertised`, check it against `iso15693_3_get_block_data(target, block)` -- `target` is in scope at `:658` and the accessor is already used at `:530`. Non-zero: keep the bit and count it, since it provably existed, provably held data, and provably wasn't cleared. Zero: drop as now.

One residual, worth a comment rather than code: if the degradation predates activation the cache is zeros there too and the block is still dropped. Smaller hole, different symptoms, and this fix doesn't close it -- better said than left implied.

`sweep_truncated` never reaches this screen, and this is the card the clock was added for.

`ISO15693_POLLER_WIPE_MAX_MS`'s own comment names it: "A card that refuses the write and still serves a read at every address never accumulates a run, so it walks all 256 blocks." On exactly that card nothing accepts a zero-write, so `wiped == 0` short-circuits here to `Fail` -> `NothingWiped` -> "No blocks could be cleared -- the card accepted no zero-write."

About 40% of the block space was ever attempted, and the flag that says so is set, plumbed all the way into `iso15693_result`, and not read. The CHANGELOG claim -- "a wipe cut short by that limit says so rather than presenting the range it reached as the card's size" -- is true of the two screens that read it and false of this one.

A `\nStopped: time limit` line matching `write_fail.c:130` closes it.

This is the only place in the app that reads `sweep_truncated`, and it's the one screen where the flag alone isn't enough.

The Partial screen prints `blocks_total` as the denominator -- which on a truncated sweep is the cut point, not the card -- and never prints `blocks_advertised`. A card claiming 64, cut at block 45 with 5 refusals:

```
Wiped 40/45 blocks
Not cleared: 5
Stopped: time limit
```

Blocks 45..63 were never attempted, still hold the previous card's data, and have no bitmap bits -- so Details omits them too. The screen names 5 residual blocks when there are 24, and there's no way for the user to learn the sweep covered 45 of a claimed 64. WipeComplete shows both figures; this shows neither.

Free, and no extra line: make the qualifier `"\nStopped at %u of %u"` with `blocks_total` / `blocks_advertised`.

Third of the four wipe screens with no truncation note. `uid_changed` pre-empts the Partial reason code, so a sweep that was both cut short and moved the UID presents the cut range as the card's extent -- which is what `sweep_truncated`'s own doc at `iso15693_poller.h:148-150` says it exists to prevent.

`:319-329` already carries the comment explaining that `wipe_uid_changed` was added to the Details gate *because* it pre-empts Partial. The new flag didn't get the same treatment.

The fix has to be Details, not a fourth line here -- see my note at `:70`; a 4th line would clip the button box, so the "no room" conclusion is right even though its stated arithmetic isn't. `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_partial_details.c` already has a caveat section (`used_gen1`, `identity_failed`); one more entry there plus `sweep_truncated` in the Details gate covers this screen and the Partial one at once.

Narrow to reach, so not blocking on its own -- but it's free once you're editing the details scene for the Partial finding.

This loop is the one that didn't get a clock, and `65d71105` is what makes that matter.

`78e1d168` bounded the wipe sweep at 10s on the argument that a long un-abortable window is a real cost. `65d71105` then killed Back for the whole ISO15693 write, clone included. `write_source_blocks` is bounded only by the source block count, and its presence check is at `:614` -- after the loop, not inside it.

Card slips off one block into a 79-block clone: every remaining block runs 3 x `write_block`, each burning the full `ISO15693_3_FDT_WRITE_POLL_FC` (271200 fc = 20ms) with no responder, plus 3 x `furi_delay_ms(5)`. About 75ms/block, 78 blocks, so roughly **6 seconds** of frozen "Writing / Don't move..." with Back dead, before the inventory at `:614` finally reports CardLost. A 256-block source is ~19s.

It terminates, so it isn't a hang, and I'm not calling it blocking. But your own Back comment argues the clone is the worse case -- "Worse for a clone, which has a `NfcCommandReset` between the UID write and the data pass" -- and it's the one left unbounded. If 10s is the right order of magnitude for how long a user may be locked on a popup, the same deadline belongs here.

Cheapest version is the sweep's own pattern: one `furi_get_tick()` before the loop, one check at the top of the body. A cut clone is a `Partial` whose unreached blocks are already in the bitmap.

The argument for not raising an error here is right and I'm not asking you to change it -- turning "user lifted the card the instant the wipe finished" into an error on every gen2 wipe would be worse than the gap it closes.

What doesn't follow is saying *nothing*. At the moment this renders, the app knows the UID check did not run -- and it renders "Wipe complete" with the success chime and a Finish button anyway. The only record is a `FURI_LOG_W` the user can't see.

A `uid_verified` flag, set false here and in the no-return branch at `:1188`, rendered as "UID not re-checked." on the wipe screen's third line: costs nothing, keeps the success tone if you want it, and stops the app asserting a check it skipped.

This is the sharper half of my note at `:1125`, because the two branches are not equally likely to be a lift.

This one fires after a *deliberate* field power-cycle, on a card that was answering a moment ago. The single most likely non-lift reason a card fails to come back is that the wipe just zeroed blocks 56/57 on an armed gen1 card -- which is precisely what `Iso15693WriteStateVerifyWipe` was created to detect. That case currently reports a clean success with a success chime.

The 15-activation budget is the right call and I'm not asking you to raise it. Worth noting the direction, though: narrowing the window makes this branch easier to hit, not harder. `:69-70` already anticipates the card that needs longer and offers the log line as the tell -- a user-visible tell costs one line.

A cut-short wipe gets the error tone and the "Wipe stopped" title, then a lone **Finish**.

This is the one wipe outcome where re-running is the correct user action -- real data may sit unwiped above the cut, which by `ISO15693_POLLER_WIPE_MAX_MS`'s own asymmetry argument is the privacy failure the sweep exists to remove -- and it's the outcome with no route back except navigating the menu again. `card_lost` gets Retry/Exit at `:286-300`; a cut sweep has at least as good a claim to it.

This rationale doesn't survive the exit `78e1d168` added. The drop is justified as removing "the space above the card's real top", which holds for the capacity break at `:850` and for the 256 ceiling, and not for the clock break at `:715` -- there the sweep ended at an arbitrary block.

Concretely: advertised 200, physical 200, dead stretch from block 150, clock fires at 155. `absent_run == 5`, so the presence check at `:800` never ran (it needs `% 8 == 0`) and the run never reached the re-probe. This loop clears bits 150..154. `blocks_total = 150`, `failed_count == 0` -> Success -> "Wipe stopped / Cleared 150 blocks / Card claims 200 / Time limit reached."

No number is wrong -- those blocks were never counted, and the truncation flag carries the honesty. But up to `ABSENT_RUN - 1` attempted-and-refused blocks below the advertised count are discarded under a rule about blocks above the card's top, and Details omits them. Either skip the drop when `wipe_truncated`, or say in the comment that the flag is what carries this path.

Same sentence in `CHANGELOG.md:74-75`.

Dead cross-reference, created by this delta: `ad4272c4` moved the read-back into `Iso15693WriteStateVerifyWipe` (`:1104`). Nothing at the end of the wipe branch (`:959-986`) reads a UID any more. Same pointer at `:695`.

Second copy of the dead pointer from `:260` -- "the read-back at the end of the Wipe branch of write_step" is now `Iso15693WriteStateVerifyWipe`.

Worth more than a find-and-replace here, because this paragraph is the OPEN QUESTION's conclusion: the whole "what IS done is the grounded half" argument now rests on a check that runs behind a field power-cycle, which is what makes it able to observe a gen1 latch at all. That's the strongest the paragraph has ever been -- it should say so.

Two figures here contradict `:56`, which gives the same 40-error budget as "roughly a 5-7 second timeout" -- i.e. 125-175ms per failed activation. This block says the full budget is "four seconds" and that 15 is "~1.5s", both of which assume 100ms.

Settled by disassembly rather than argument: `iso15693_3_poller_run` calls `furi_delay_ms(100)` on every failed activation. Exactly 100ms, plus each attempt's own airtime. So your two new figures are consistent with each other and `:56` is the one that's wrong.

Worth fixing rather than leaving as an oddity, because `:69-70` tells a future maintainer to raise this constant from bench observation -- they'll want the right ms-per-error to reason with.

Three waits, not two. The retry loop at `:731-735` has no `break` before the final `furi_delay_ms`, so a block failing all three attempts pays 3 x `ISO15693_POLLER_VERIFY_RETRY_MS` = 15ms. `:159` -- same file, 22 lines down -- has it right: "three refused writes, three 5ms waits and one refused read."

The error is in your favour: correcting it lowers the derived per-frame cost, so "256 blocks all accepting -> 3-4s" gains margin rather than losing it. The conclusion survives; the arithmetic doesn't.

The neighbours check out, for what it's worth -- `:126-127` ("10-18 seconds") and `:134` ("roughly the 18s above") both reproduce cleanly at 256 x 40-70ms. Only `:137-139` needs the edit.

The conclusion holds and I've said so up top -- this is about the supporting sentences, because this comment is what a future maintainer will widen or narrow the swallow from.

- **"ISO15693 is the only poller here that guarantees one"** -- not so. gen1a's write error sets `Gen1aPollerStateFail` (`gen1a_poller.c:241-246`) and the next tick runs `gen1a_poller_fail_handler` (`:324-332`) -> `Fail`. USCUID-**backdoor** returns `NfcCommandContinue` on a write error (`uscuid_ul_poller.c:383`) and walks the remaining pages to `Partial`/`Fail` (`:317-327`). Both run on raw `nfc_start`, where `NfcEventTypePollerReady` is a poll-cycle tick rather than an activation -- which is exactly why the missing error budget doesn't strand them.
- **"gen2, Classic, gen4 and USCUID-direct advance one block/page per Ready"** -- Classic isn't a separate poller (`:272-275` starts the gen2 one, so it's gen2 counted twice), gen4 writes its MFU signature/version/password tail in a single callback (`gen4_poller.c:462-565`), and gen1a and USCUID-backdoor also advance one per Ready. So the list isn't the distinguishing property it's presented as.

The genuine stranding cases are gen2/Classic (halts after every block, `gen2_poller.c:523-524`, forcing a re-activation that then fails) and USCUID-direct (the `NfcCommandReset` at `uscuid_ul_poller.c:379-382`) -- which is precisely what your bench table found. Narrowing those two sentences to that is all it needs; the "no activation-error budget" observation is accurate on all four, it's just the inference from it that over-reaches.

Separately, `:521-522` cites only `ISO15693_POLLER_MAX_ACTIVATION_ERRORS` -> CardLost, but `ad4272c4` added a second budget in this same PR whose exhaustion reports the wipe *result*, not CardLost (`iso15693_poller.c:1184-1196`). The guarantee still holds; the justification should describe both.

The rows-52-63 half is exactly right. The 4th-line half isn't, and it's repeated verbatim at `:188-190` and `:213-214`.

From the firmware: `elements_multiline_text_aligned` advances y by `canvas_current_font_height()` per line, which for FontSecondary (haxrcorp4089) returns the font's `max_char_height` 0x0a **+1 = 11**, not 9. `elements_button_left` does `canvas_draw_box(canvas, 0, height-12, w, 12)` -> rows 52-63.

So at y=13 the line tops land at 13 / 24 / 35 / **46** / 57. A 4th line occupies rows 46-55: its bottom four rows fall inside the button box, across the button's width. Compromised rather than "overpainted" -- and line 5 at y=57 is the one fully buried.

The sibling at `:122` (body at y=20, "only three FontSecondary lines fit") reproduces exactly: tops 20/31/42, 3rd line bottom at 51, 4th at 53 fully inside the box. Almost certainly where this text came from, without redoing it for the higher origin.

No visible bug -- all three branches emit at most 3 lines. But the constraint is load-bearing: it's the stated reason the UID-changed screen at `:196` has nowhere to put a truncation note. It genuinely doesn't, so the conclusion is right for the wrong reason and the fix belongs in Details either way.

"a clean success" is wrong for the truncated case, which shares this reason code. `nfc_magic_scene_write.c:396-405` routes every wipe Success here, and a clock-cut sweep with no failed blocks still reports Success -- the screen then renders "Wipe stopped" with `sequence_error` (`write_fail.c:43`, `:63`).

`78e1d168` added truncation without revisiting the comment `241d3957` had just written.

This says a wipe Success means "every block the card answered for is clear, **and** the UID read back as the one it presented". Neither half is unconditional any more:

- Success is reported when the card never returns from the power-cycle, with no UID observed at all (`iso15693_poller.c:1188-1196`)
- Success is reported for a clock-cut sweep, where blocks above the cut were never attempted (`:711-716`)

Callers are expected to consult `sweep_truncated` for the second -- and this enum is the contract, so it should say so.

Edited in this delta for the power-cycle, but still describes the absent-run as the sweep's only stop condition, and lists the reported events with no mention of `sweep_truncated` -- which the same header documents on the result struct at `:147-150`. A caller reading only this doc has no way to learn a wipe can stop on a clock.

Also `:214` ends a paragraph on a two-word orphan line ("...promising one. A card") left by the reflow.

"neither of which is a fault" is too strong now. The screen's own comment at `write_fail.c:49-50` names a third cause -- "a dead stretch below the advertised count that never recovers" -- and the clock cut is a fourth. Both *are* faults, and the first is my blocking finding.

`nfc_magic_app_i.h:131-133` carries the same overreach ("neither direction is a fault"), reasoning only from the CFG-programming cause.

Two smaller ones in this section:
- `:34-38` -- "attempts every block the card claims even where a stretch of them answers nothing" is contradicted three lines later by "It is bounded by a time limit as well as by the 256-block ceiling", inside the same bullet.
- `:74-75` repeats the tail-drop premise I've flagged at `iso15693_poller.c:853`.

**Simplify, minor, and both free.**

`furi_ms_to_ticks(ISO15693_POLLER_WIPE_MAX_MS)` is recomputed on every one of up to 256 iterations from two compile-time constants. Hoist it beside `sweep_start`. Keep the comparison in its current elapsed form (`furi_get_tick() - sweep_start > budget`) -- that's tick-wraparound safe and an absolute `deadline` would not be.

Related, at `:799`: `block + 1 < advertised` makes the reader re-derive the off-by-one every time, while the comment above already states the rule in words. `const bool claimed_range_attempted = (block + 1 >= advertised);` then `if(!claimed_range_attempted)` puts the words in the code.

"every exit" isn't quite -- the two card-lost paths (`:803`, `:813`) `return` from the function and skip this entirely, so a card-lost wipe is never timed.

Since the stated purpose is "so the wall-clock cost of a sweep is measurable on any card", that's the interesting gap rather than a wording nit: the lifted-card case is the one where you'd most want to know how long the app spent before noticing.
